<div class="datom-callout datom-callout-goal" markdown="1">
**Goal:** a working datom project in a few minutes, with no GitHub account, no
token and no cloud account. Everything lives in folders on your machine, and
this article runs as written.
</div>

A datom project has two parts: a **git repo** that records every change, and
**storage** that holds the data itself. Both can be folders:

- the git repo is a *bare* git repo in a folder (one with no working files,
  which is what a git server holds), and datom creates it for you;
- storage is a folder too, through `datom_store_local()`.

A folder repo needs no token. Point both at a shared network drive and a
small team can work this way. For GitHub, see [Getting Started](getting-started.html);
for S3, see [Starting on S3](start-on-s3.html).

## Pick the folders

```{r folders}
library(datom)

home      <- file.path(tempdir(), "datom-try")
remote    <- file.path(home, "study-001.git")  # the git repo; datom creates it
storage   <- file.path(home, "storage")        # where the data goes
workspace <- file.path(home, "study-001")      # your working copy
dir.create(home)
```

Temporary folders keep the article tidy. For real work, use folders that last,
and for a team, folders everyone can reach.

## Start the project

A store with a folder address is a writer store, with no token:

```{r store}
store <- datom_store(
  data          = datom_store_local(path = storage),
  data_repo_url = remote
)
store$role
```

`create_repo = TRUE` makes the bare repo at that address. Its parent folder must
already exist; datom never creates parents, so a typo stops here rather than
creating a stray folder.

```{r init}
datom_init_repo(workspace, project_name = "STUDY_001", store = store,
                create_repo = TRUE)
```

## Write and read a table

```{r write-read}
conn <- datom_get_conn(path = workspace, store = store)

datom_write(conn, data = datom_example_data("dm"), name = "dm",
            message = "First extract")

dm <- datom_read(conn, "dm")
nrow(dm)
datom_list(conn)[, c("name", "current_version")]
```

## A second writer

A colleague who can reach both folders clones the project with the same store:

```{r clone}
colleague <- datom_clone(file.path(home, "study-001-colleague"), store)
datom_list(colleague)$name
```

## A reader

A reader needs only the storage folder: no git, no repo address.

```{r reader}
reader_store <- datom_store(data = datom_store_local(path = storage))
reader <- datom_get_conn(store = reader_store, project_name = "STUDY_001")
identical(datom_read(reader, "dm"), dm)
```

## What is not supported yet

- **SSH addresses** (`git@github.com:...` or `ssh://...`) stop with a message.
  Pushing over SSH would use your SSH agent's keys, and datom never picks up a
  credential on its own. Use an `https://` address with a token, or a folder.
- **Moving a project from a folder to GitHub** has no supported route yet. To
  start on GitHub, follow [Getting Started](getting-started.html).

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
unlink(home, recursive = TRUE)
```
